    Engineering

    Project-specific loading information

    Ground snow load — NZS 1170.3
    Fixed first-release basis: Importance Level 2, 50-year design working life; ULS annual probability 1/150 (kp 1.25) and SLS 1/25 (kp 0.84).
    ULS ground snow load—
    SLS ground snow load—
    Calculation details, sources and notes
    Map suggestion—
    Terrain class—
    ULS equation result—
    Snow density—
    Result basisSelect the applicable snow region and choose a site.
    SourcesAS/NZS 1170.3 metadata · MBIE B1/VM1 clarification
    Design noteThe suggested region is a screening interpretation of the approximate boundaries in AS/NZS 1170.3:2003 Figure 2.2, not an authoritative GIS layer. The user retains final region selection. Ground snow load is not roof snow load: roof shape, exposure, accumulation, drifting and other coefficients still need to be applied. Confirm elevation and any more onerous territorial-authority requirement. Sites above 1,800 m and avalanche-prone sites require specific assessment.
    Equivalent-static site hazard spectrum — NZS 1170.5
    Initial scope: site hazard spectrum only. The defaults are IL2/50-year screening choices (ULS 1/500 and SLS 1/25), but the annual probabilities, site class, Z and major-fault distance must be confirmed by the designer.
    ULS C(T₁), equivalent static—
    SLS C(T₁), equivalent static—
    Calculation details, sources and notes
    Locality suggestion—

    SLS near-fault, N(T,D)—
    Result basisSelect a hazard factor and site subsoil class.
    SourcesNZS 1170.5:2004 · B1/VM1 Second Edition · MBIE locality Z table
    Design noteThis reports the horizontal equivalent-static elastic site hazard spectrum C(T) = Ch(T)ZR N(T,D), using the main Table 3.1 ordinates; it does not calculate base shear, modal/time-history spectra or a design action coefficient. Regional geology does not establish site class. The displayed active-fault distance is used only when its name matches one of the eleven major faults in Table 3.6, and remains a screening trace distance rather than a confirmed fault-plane distance. Liquefaction, slope instability and surface fault rupture are outside this calculation.
    Site wind speed — AS/NZS 1170.2:2021
    Calculation: Vsit,β = VRMcMd(Mz,catMsMt). Hill shape can be screened from the terrain model and remains editable; terrain category, shielding, lee zone and wind direction remain designer inputs.
    Region suggestionChoose a site, then confirm the region against Figure 3.1(B).

    Select a site to sample four 15 km terrain transects and assess eight wind directions.

    Runs only when you press the button. The sampled coordinates are sent to the public Open-Meteo elevation service (Copernicus GLO-90), with OpenTopoData NZ DEM 8 m used as a fallback.

    Site wind speed, Vsit,β—
    Velocity pressure—
    Calculation details, source and notes
    Regional speed, VR—
    Terrain multiplier, Mz,cat—
    Topographic multiplier, Mt—
    Result basisSelect and confirm the wind region and terrain category.
    SourceAS/NZS 1170.2:2021
    Design noteThis is an auditable site-wind-speed calculation, not a complete wind-action design. Automatic topography samples the exact cardinal axes at 250 m spacing; it does not search every cross-section within ±22.5°, reliably classify escarpments, or replace surveyed terrain and engineering review. Confirm the wind-region boundary, recurrence interval, terrain averaging, shielding geometry, governing hill or escarpment section, and New Zealand lee-zone extent against the licensed Standard. Velocity pressure is shown only as 0.0006V² kPa; aerodynamic coefficients and structural actions are not applied.

    Natural hazards

    Published local and regional council hazard mapping

    Choose a site to check connected Otago, Waikato and Bay of Plenty regional hazard layers.
    InterpretationA flag means published mapping intersects the selected point or a mapped study applies there. It is not a property-specific risk assessment. “No polygon returned” does not prove the hazard is absent; check the linked source, the relevant city or district council, the LIM and specialist advice.
